---
title: "6 · Probability and Variational Autoencoders"
code-tools: false
toc: false
---

Learning a probability distribution from data alone, and drawing new samples from it. Why an autoencoder cannot generate, and the probability toolkit needed to fix it: distributions and densities, expectations as averages over samples, the Gaussian, joint, conditional and marginal distributions, Bayes' rule, the Kullback–Leibler divergence and maximum likelihood, latent-variable models. The variational autoencoder: training and sampling, the decoder as a likelihood, binary cross-entropy, the evidence lower bound, the reparametrisation trick, the latent space. Conditional generation of a chosen digit or cell type, checked with classifiers trained on real or synthetic data, and disentangled latent features with the β-VAE.
